source.title: Counterfactual Influence as a Distributional Quantity
source.authors: Matthieu Meeus; Igor Shilov; Georgios Kaissis; Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how training examples influence predictions and compares influence with extractability for unique and near-duplicate records. These results bear on memorization and a related training-versus-held-out result, but do not test the claim versions about generalization gaps, optimizers, architecture comparisons, or sharpness.
record.gate_note: The paper’s main influence and extractability results concern memorization, not the specified generalization-gap versions. Appendix A reports training and held-out loss/BLEU during GPT-NEO fine-tuning; Appendix D reports CIFAR-10 train and validation curves, but the text provides no numerical curve values, and neither appendix tests a listed version. No rows for the cited related-work findings.
record.test_reason: The study measures counterfactual influence, approximate extraction, and near-duplicate identification. None tests V1–V8. In particular, marginal effects on training targets do not test V8's claim about test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples. The appendix learning curves do not supply the comparisons required by any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that near-duplicates can reduce self-influence while increasing approximate extractability, and that full influence distributions reveal memorization patterns missed by self-influence alone.
record.recipe_differences: Measures counterfactual influence distributions and extractability rather than training recipes or generalization-gap interventions.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-NEO records with near-duplicates have lower mean self-influence (0.495 versus 1.410) but higher approximate-extraction BLEU (0.363 versus 0.070) than unique records.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-influence alone can understate approximate extractability when training records have near-duplicates.

fits_no_version.finding: For selected CIFAR-10 targets with low influence margins, the most influential distinct training image is described as a visual near-duplicate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Full counterfactual influence distributions can reveal near-duplicates in image training data.

record.problems: The detailed influence and extractability comparison uses one small language model and artificially crafted near-duplicates. CIFAR-10 near-duplicate evidence is presented through selected targets and figures rather than an aggregate quantified comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Appendix A and Appendix D plot training and held-out or validation curves but give no textual numerical result bearing on a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes and regularization regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of generalization gaps relative to other measures.
Test-accuracy changes after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The use of counterfactual influence extends a framework associated with V8's original source; it does not test or rely on V8's removal-and-test-accuracy finding. No verdict labels are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare random-label fitting with natural-label generalization or report the specified architecture and recipe conditions.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
Does not test magnitude-aware sharpness or compare gap measures.
Does not remove memorized examples and retrain to assess test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured the Top-1 Influence Margin and inspected the most influential distinct sample for selected targets.

conditions.value: target with smallest IM among samples whose self-influence exceeded the median

rows.measure: Self-influence and influence of most influential distinct sample, with a plotted influence distribution
rows.value: Figure labels give I(xt ⇒ xt) = 0.6680 and I(xi ⇒ xt) = 0.6681; text identifies the distinct sample as a natural visual near-duplicate.
rows.note: The finding concerns near-duplicate detection through influence distributions, not a listed claim version.
rows.check: The influence values match Figure 2. This is a deliberately selected illustrative target with the smallest influence margin among targets above median self-influence, not an aggregate estimate of near-duplicate prevalence or a test of a listed version.
